title: Share bounded dynamic-tool wire mechanics across diagnostic, child, GUI and settings adapters
evidence: Full bodies reviewed. diagnostic_dynamic_tools.rs:1230-1246,1333-1424 and diagnostic_child_dynamic_tools.rs:720-730,789-818,848-855,892-929,1067-1085 repeat closed argument types, schemas, serialization and byte truncation. GUI equivalents are at gui_control_dynamic_tools.rs:329-350,436-464; settings response.rs:1-50 repeats response envelope and encoding mechanics.

Repeated success/error responses use ok/result or ok/error, with kind/message/tool/callId error fields. Leaf policies differ: child namespace must be explicit; supervisor-side legacy diagnostics allow omitted namespace; settings empty arguments may normalize null; GUI excessive limits reject while diagnostics clamp.
proposal: Introduce a small private tool-wire module using existing serde/serde_json for compact response encoding, parameterized UTF-8-safe byte truncation, identical closed-object schemas and identical argument structs. Keep thin typed error adapters and policy checks at each caller. Deserialize already admitted bounded Values by reference instead of cloning them where serde supports it. Net estimate 150-220 lines after helper declarations, imports, adapters and focused wire-contract verification; central estimate 180. This excludes error Display derives counted by AU-004 and excludes canonical streaming argument parsers.
required_contract_changes: None for the compatible extraction. Preserve namespace admission, target identity, distinct 512/1024-byte caps, missing/null behavior, exact envelope/error wording, strict unknown-field handling and each limit policy. Do not apply whole-Value parsing to conversation, lifecycle or branch-resolution ingress.
verification: Implementation should retain existing diagnostic/settings/GUI tool tests and compare valid and invalid envelopes, Unicode truncation edges, namespace omission, unknown fields, null/empty inputs, exact target mismatch and per-tool limit behavior. Add only uncovered shared-helper boundary cases.

title: Consolidate small repeated diagnostic ring mechanics only if the helper remains smaller
evidence: Full bodies reviewed. Three logs at diagnostic_dynamic_tools.rs:552-584,662-759 repeat next_sequence, capacity, VecDeque construction, saturating assignment and oldest-first eviction. Result filtering at 1276-1319 repeats after-sequence then limit handling; scroll summaries require recomputation after filtering.
Typed record sanitization and three typed snapshot products are meaningful; most of the visible snapshot code remains necessary after extraction.
proposal: Evaluate one private const-capacity sequenced ring with a narrow record interface, retaining typed log facades and snapshot assembly. Reuse only the identical filter/truncate primitive where it pays for its callback/interface cost. Conservative net estimate 20-40 lines after generic declarations, typed adapters and verification; central estimate 30. Treat this as a low-priority local cleanup, not a substantial new framework. Do not include snapshot demand or shell count/projection changes already covered by AS7.
required_contract_changes: None. Preserve independent sequence domains starting at one, saturating increment, capacities, bounded strings, chronological results, cursor semantics, snapshot next_sequence and post-filter continuity recomputation.
verification: On implementation, retain ring eviction, saturated cursor, UTF-8 sanitization and scroll-continuity tests; compare snapshots before and after filtering. Reject the extraction if final helper and adapters exceed deleted code.

title: Define common memory milestone log fields once
evidence: Full bodies reviewed. memory_diagnostics.rs:229-502 builds retained-state aliases and repeats the same retained diagnostic fields in success and OS-counter failure events at 349-423 and 426-499. Both branches also emit retained_state using Debug.

Success includes numeric private/working-set/pagefile counters; failure emits memory_counters_available=false and the error. tests/memory_diagnostics.rs verifies disabled logging does not evaluate retained-state construction.
proposal: Use one local field-list emission macro with branch-specific counter/error fields and message arguments, preserving both existing event schemas. Keep common field conversion and lazy enabled checks. Net estimate 60-85 lines after macro and focused event-schema verification; central estimate 70. A larger 200-plus-line deletion could remove all flattened aliases in favor of retained_state, but that changes diagnostic consumer format and is not included in this estimate. This does not count AS7 shell-side retained-count projection work.
required_contract_changes: None for preserving the two event schemas. Removing flat field aliases instead would require explicit diagnostics output-contract and consumer changes; that alternative remains unapproved.
verification: On implementation, capture success and unavailable events to compare field names, value types, messages and content-free payload; keep the disabled-evaluation test. Preserve Windows counter meanings and unavailable behavior on other targets.

title: Retain diagnostic child process ownership rather than adopting process-wrap
evidence: Full bodies and platform branches reviewed. supervisor.rs:831-902 configures a Windows kernel job with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE and explicit termination/release; the rest of the supervisor retains protocol handshake, process identity, cleanup failure custody and bounded readiness/stop behavior.

Tagged process-wrap v10.0.0 std/job_object.rs:97 calls make_job_object(handle, false); the public JobObject is a unit struct and job port is private. Exact upstream source was checked 2026-09-06 and agrees with the existing backend dependency investigation.
proposal: Retain the current app supervisor. process-wrap could replace only the small OS job wrapper, and its synchronous API lacks the required kernel kill-on-close configuration. A new custom wrapper/fork plus typed error and cleanup adapters would erase the already modest line savings; no removal estimate is claimed. Generic RPC or async task frameworks likewise do not replace Beryl's identity and custody protocol.
required_contract_changes: Adopting the currently inspected synchronous API would require weakening kernel owner-exit cleanup or introducing a maintained custom fork; neither is recommended.
verification: Audit only; no processes launched or tests run.
Retain current real child handshake and cleanup failure tests. No new package, target, background process or temporary resource was created.
